identity.title: Resolving the extended atmosphere and the inner wind of Mira (o Ceti) with long ALMA baselines

paper_type_evidence.quote: The prototypical Mira variable, $o$ Cet (Mira), has been observed as a Science Verification target in the 2014 ALMA Long Baseline Campaign, offering the first opportunity to study these physical conditions in detail.

targets.name: Mira A (o Ceti) and Mira B

evidence.quote: The distance of the Mira AB system was estimated to be $110{\pm}9$ pc (cite: haniff1995)
We have determined the centre of Mira A's continuum emission to be at $(\text{RA}, \text{Dec}) = (02^{\rm h}19^{\rm m}20{s}795

question.value: What are the physical conditions (density, temperature, SiO/H2O abundance, infall/outflow velocities) in Mira's extended atmosphere and inner wind, as probed by long-baseline ALMA continuum and SiO/H2O lines, and how do hydrodynamical models compare?

evidence.quote: We derive the gas density, kinetic temperature, molecular abundance and outflow/infall velocities in Mira's extended atmosphere by modelling the SiO and H$_2$O lines.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA\#2011.0.00014.SV.

bands.value: Band 3 and Band 6 observed; Band 6 (229 GHz) lines analysed

evidence.quote: The Mira AB system was observed with ALMA on 2014 October 17 and 25 (ALMA Band 3) and on 2014 October 29 and November 1 (ALMA Band 6)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Band 6: continuum window at 229.6 GHz plus six 117.2 MHz line windows; channel 122.1 kHz (SiO), 61.0 kHz (H2O, H30alpha)

evidence.quote: In Band 6, a continuum window at 229.6 GHz together with six spectral line windows of 117.2 MHz bandwidth around $^{28}$SiO ${\varv} = 0,1,2$ $J=5-4$
The shortest baselines (and the maximum number of antennae) in the observations of Bands 3 and 6 are $29.07\,{\rm m}$ (38) and $15.23\,{\rm m}$ (39), respectively.
With the longest baseline of 15 km, ALMA produces clearly resolved images of the continuum and molecular line emission/absorption at an angular resolution of ${\sim}30\,{\rm mas}$ at 220 GHz.
The maximum recoverable scales[^3] of the SiO lines in Bands 3 and 6 are therefore ${\sim}14{\ensuremath{''}}8$ and ${\sim}11{\ensuremath{''}}3$, respectively
on 2014 October 29 and November 1 (ALMA Band 6) as part of the 2014 ALMA Long Baseline Campaign Science Verification

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: ALMA Science Verification data, calibrated by JAO/ARC staff

evidence.quote: The SV data had been calibrated by staff members of the Joint ALMA Observatory (JAO) and the ALMA Regional Centres (ARCs)

provided.value: visual light-curve data used to derive stellar phase (~0.45)

evidence.quote: Based on the visual magnitude data reported by the AAVSO, the stellar phase of Mira A is ${\sim}0.45$ at the time of this observation

what.value: CODEX o54 model atmosphere structures (density, temperature, velocity) provided by developers

evidence.quote: From the CODEX developers we have obtained the atmospheric structure information of the `o54` model series

external_data_from_literature.citation: Ireland et al. 2008, 2011; Scholz et al. 2014 (cite: ireland2008; ireland2011; scholz2014)

what.value: SiO-He collisional rate coefficients (scaled by 1.38 for H2)

evidence.quote: extrapolated from the scaled (by 1.38) rate coefficients between SiO–He collisions as derived by (cite: dayou2006)
we adopt the value of $R_{\star}$ to be $12.3\,{\rm mas}$ (or $292\,R_{\astrosun}$) as determined by (cite: perrin2004)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: CODEX o54 5400 Lsun hydrodynamical models at phases near 0.45 (250420, 261740, 286060, 287880, 289440, 291820) used as RATRAN inputs

evidence.quote: the models at the stellar phases closest to this 2014 ALMA SV dataset (near phase 0.45) are models 250420[^1] (phase 0.38), 261740 (0.40)

pipeline_or_manual.value: Calibrated by JAO/ARC staff; self-calibration solutions from ALMA Science Portal applied

evidence.quote: We downloaded the self-calibration solutions from the ALMA Science Portal and applied them to the preliminarily calibrated data, and then imaged the continuum and spectral line data.
We use CASA version 4.2.2 for the self-calibration and imaging
The real uncertainty of the flux is dominated by the absolute flux calibration, which is estimated to be of order 20%.

self_calibration.value: Continuum solutions for continuum; strongest channels of SiO v=1 maser for line data

evidence.quote: from the strongest spectral channels of the $^{28}$SiO ${\varv} = 1$ data, which exhibits strong maser emission, for the spectral line data

task.value: CASA clean (Clark); continuum-subtracted and non-subtracted cubes

evidence.quote: The spectral line image data cubes of the SiO and H$_2$O lines in ALMA Band 6 were created by the image deconvolution task, `clean`, in CASA.
We weighted the visibilities with a robust (Briggs) parameter of $\mathcal{R}_{\rm Briggs}=0.5$
The cell size and total size of the images are $0{\ensuremath{''}}005 \times 0{\ensuremath{''}}005$ and $15{\ensuremath{''}} \times 15{\ensuremath{''}}$, respectively.
$0{\ensuremath{''}}005 \times 0{\ensuremath{''}}005$ and $15{\ensuremath{''}} \times 15{\ensuremath{''}}$, respectively.

continuum_subtraction.value: uvcontsub linear polynomial on line-free channels; but modelling uses non-subtracted cubes

evidence.quote: The continuum was subtracted, with the `uvcontsub` task in CASA, by fitting a linear polynomial to the real and imaginary parts of the visibility data of the line-free (i.e., continuum-only) channels in each spectral window.

primary_beam_correction.value: not needed (primary beam ~28" at 220 GHz) except Fig. 1

evidence.quote: At 220 GHz, the primary beam FWHM of the 12-m array is about $28\ensuremath{''}$, which is much larger than the size of the line emission/absorption, and therefore no primary beam correction is needed.
We restored the images with a circular beam of FWHM $0{\ensuremath{''}}032$ for the $^{28}$SiO and $^{29}$SiO lines, and of FWHM $0{\ensuremath{''}}030$ for the H$_2$O $v_2=1$ line.

final_rms.value: CLEAN threshold ~2-3 mJy/beam (~1.5x rms); sigma = 0.80 mJy/beam in SiO v=0 maps

evidence.quote: CLEANed the images down to a threshold of ${\sim}2$–$3\,{\rm mJy}\,{\rm beam}^{-1}$, which is about 1.5 times the rms noise level.

what.value: Calibration scripts, self-cal solutions and example imaging script from ALMA SV data package

evidence.quote: Detailed calibration scripts, preliminarily calibrated data products (i.e., without self-calibration), and self-calibration solutions for both continuum and spectral line data are available at the ALMA Science Portal

inherited.from_reference: ALMA Science Portal SV data / ALMA Partnership 2015 (cite: lbc2014)

what.value: Continuum two-component model (uniform disk + Gaussian) following earlier analyses

evidence.quote: The choices of model components are the similar to those adopted by (cite: mrm2015) and (cite: vro2015).

inherited.from_reference: Matthews et al. 2015; Vlemmings et al. 2015

unstated_but_needed: Exact line-free channel ranges used in uvcontsub (only said to differ from CASA Guide script)
Exact clean parameters (niter, masks, spw/channel regridding) and which self-cal tables
Full numerical RATRAN input profiles (density, T, velocity, abundance power-law indices) for Model 3
RATRAN grid, photon count and convergence settings
Formal fitting/goodness-of-fit method for the models (fit by eye, no stated metric)
CODEX file contents are private (provided by developers)

analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and fit continuum visibilities

method.value: Fit uniform disk / Gaussian models to Band 6 continuum visibilities for Mira A and B

evidence.quote: We fit the visibilities with the task `uvfit` (Revision 1.10, 2013 August) in Miriad.

validation.value: Cross-checked uvfit with CASA uvmodelfit and UVMULTIFIT

evidence.quote: We have cross-checked the $uv$-fitting results from the respective tasks in Miriad and CASA with single-component models, and both tasks return similar results.

analysis_steps.goal: Image SiO and H2O line cubes and extract spectra

method.value: clean without continuum subtraction; spectra extracted at centre and at radii 32-160 mas along PA 0, 90, 180, 270 deg

evidence.quote: We have extracted the SiO and H$_2$O spectra from the centre of Mira's continuum, and from an array of positions at radii 0$''$032, 0$''$064, 0$''$096, 0$''$128 and 0$''$160

validation.value: Compared continuum-subtracted vs full-data spectra; CASA simulobserve test showed spurious bumps from CLEAN

evidence.quote: we conclude that the "bump" in the continuum-subtracted spectrum is indeed a spurious feature introduced during the imaging (CLEAN) process.

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer modelling of SiO and H2O spectra

method.value: 1-D RATRAN Monte Carlo models with power-law density/temperature, SiO two-step abundance, pseudo-continuum core, mixed infall/outflow velocity (Model 3); models convolved with the clean beam and compared by eye

evidence.quote: RATRAN solves the coupled level population and radiative transfer equations with the Monte Carlo method and generates an output image cube for each of the modelled lines.
$R_{\rm continuum} = 3.60 \times 10^{13}\,{\rm cm}$ (21.8 mas) and $2600\,{\rm K}$, respectively.

key_parameters.value: SiO abundance drop at r_cond = 1.0e14 cm (~5 R*), outer ~1% of inner; H2O abundance 5.0e-6 (5.0e-5 near photosphere)

evidence.quote: The radius at which SiO abundance drops significantly is assumed to be $r_{\rm cond} = 1.0 \times 10^{14}\,{\rm cm} \approx 5\,R_{\star}$ in our preferred model.

assumptions.value: Collisional partner purely rotational ground-state H2; spherical symmetry; distance 110 pc; R* = 12.3 mas

evidence.quote: we assume that the gas in Mira's extended atmosphere is composed of purely neutral, molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) in its rotationally ground state, $J=0$.

fitting.value: Empirical trial-and-error exploration of profiles; no sampler or likelihood

evidence.quote: We have empirically explored different types of profiles that are plausible in the inner winds and circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars.

validation.value: Sensitivity tests on density, abundance, temperature; alternative infall-only Models 1 and 2 rejected

evidence.quote: We present here two models, Models 1 and 2, that fail to reproduce the observed SiO and H2O spectra around Mira in ALMA Band 6.

method.value: Use CODEX o54 density (scaled by 1e4), temperature and velocity as RATRAN inputs; modify radio-continuum radius to hide strong shocks

evidence.quote: we scale the number density of all CODEX models by a factor of $10^4$ such that the density outside the radio photosphere reaches at least $10^{12}\,{\rm cm}^{-3}$.

assumptions.value: m_part = 0.7 m_H2 + 0.3 m_He, helium mass fraction 0.3

validation.value: Qualitative comparison of synthesized and observed spectra

evidence.quote: Overall, considering the complexity of Mira’s extended atmosphere and inner wind, we believe that Model 3 can satisfactorily reproduce most of the features in the observed SiO and H$_2$O spectra in ALMA Band 6.
We use CASA version 4.2.2 for the self-calibration and imaging (except for the image binning task as mentioned below)
We fit the visibilities with the task `uvfit` (Revision 1.10, 2013 August) in Miriad.
Using CASA/`UVMULTIFIT` (version 2.1.4-r3), we also obtained the similar results as reported above.

used_for.value: 1-D radiative transfer modelling of SiO and H2O lines

evidence.quote: We have modelled the H$_2$O and SiO spectra with the radiative transfer code RATRAN
with the aid of the `matplotlib` plotting library (version 1.4.3)

used_for.value: extrapolating SiO collisional rate coefficients and building molecular datafile

evidence.quote: We use the Python libraries, NumPy[^14] (version 1.9.2) (cite: numpy) and SciPy[^15] (version 0.15.1)

results_numeric.quantity: Mira A radio photosphere brightness temperature (uniform disk)

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature of the uniform disk model of Mira A is found to be $2611 \pm 51\,{\rm K}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Mira A total continuum flux at 229.6 GHz

evidence.quote: the total flux of Mira A is $149.70 \pm 0.04\,{\rm mJy}$ and that of Mira B is $11.19 \pm 0.04\,{\rm mJy}$
we derive an independent spectral index (using the spectral line windows in Band 6 only) of $1.82 \pm 0.33$
with the shock velocity of $\Delta V \lesssim 12\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$, near the radio photosphere of Mira

results_numeric.quantity: SiO depletion radius and gas temperature

evidence.quote: gas-phase SiO starts to deplete at a radius of *at least* $4\,R_{\star}$ and a gas temperature of ${\lesssim}600\,{\rm K}$

results_numeric.quantity: Gas density just beyond radio photosphere

evidence.quote: The gas density reaches $10^{12}$–$10^{13}\,{\rm cm}^{-3}$ just beyond the radio photosphere.

The infall velocity immediately above this expanding layer is about $7.3\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$, and the expansion velocity below this layer is about $4.0\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Clumpy SiO emission within ~0.2" and an arc-like SiO feature to ~3" west

evidence.quote: the SiO vibrational ground state emission extends to a larger projected radial distance than other directions

findings_qualitative.value: No compact hotspot found in continuum, contrary to Vlemmings et al. 2015

evidence.quote: we have not found any sign of a compact (${\sim}4.7\,{\rm mas}$) hotspot ($T_b \sim 10\,000\,{\rm K}$) in Mira A's continuum

claims.hypothesis: Does Mira's millimetre continuum contain a compact bright hotspot?
claims.experiment: Visibility fitting of Band 6 continuum with Miriad uvfit and UVMULTIFIT, reproducing Vlemmings et al. approach
claims.result: Additional Gaussian is ~26 mas, not 4.7 mas; Tb(uniform disk)=2611 K
claims.finding: No evidence for a compact hotspot

evidence.quote: we have not found any sign of a compact (${\sim}4.7\,{\rm mas}$) hotspot

claims.hypothesis: What are the atmospheric structure and SiO depletion in Mira's inner wind?
claims.experiment: RATRAN modelling of SiO and H2O spectra
claims.result: Infall with shock <~12 km/s; SiO depletes beyond ~4 R* at T<~600 K
claims.finding: Inner dust shells probably not pure silicate

evidence.quote: Our modelling shows that SiO gas starts to deplete beyond $4\,R_{\star}$ and at a kinetic temperature of ${\lesssim}600\,{\rm K}$.

claims.hypothesis: Can CODEX hydrodynamical models reproduce the observed spectra?
claims.experiment: Use CODEX o54 structures as RATRAN inputs, with density scaled by 1e4
claims.result: Qualitatively reproduce spectra; after hiding strong shocks fit well
claims.finding: CODEX reproduces observations in remarkable detail; non-equilibrium models with extended hot regions not supported

evidence.quote: the synthesised spectra from the CODEX models can then reasonably well-fit the observed spectra in this SV observation

claims.hypothesis: Are the bumps in continuum-subtracted spectra real?
claims.experiment: Weighting, iteration, long-baseline tests and simobserve simulation
claims.finding: The bump is a CLEAN artefact

evidence.quote: we conclude that the "bump" in the continuum-subtracted spectrum is indeed a spurious feature introduced during the imaging (CLEAN) process.

why_this_method.value: Non-subtracted images used because continuum-subtracted deconvolution produced spurious bumps

evidence.quote: The images (and hence the spectra) deconvolved without continuum subtracted should better represent the real emission and absorption of the SiO and H$_2$O lines.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Infall-only Models 1 and 2 rejected because of excess blueshifted emission

evidence.quote: Our modelling shows that pure infall would produce too much emission in the blueshifted velocities of the spectra than is observed

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extended shock-heated layer (~4000 K) from non-equilibrium models rejected

evidence.quote: the synthesised spectra exhibit very strong emission features that are absent in the data.

limitations_admitted.value: 1-D model ignores clumps; collisional rate coefficients incomplete (no H, e-, excited H2), so density and abundance uncertain

evidence.quote: the derived H$_2$ gas density from our RATRAN modelling is just a proxy of the densities of all possible collisional partners of SiO

limitations_admitted.value: Clumpy structure in images may not all be real

evidence.quote: the simulated ALMA observation suggests that the clumpy structures in the extended atmosphere and inner wind of Mira may not be all real.

referee_caveats_inferred: No formal fit or goodness-of-fit; models adjusted by eye, so parameters have no uncertainties
Single-epoch snapshot; CODEX comparison needed arbitrary 1e4 density scaling and moved continuum radius
CLEAN artefacts leave imaging reliability uncertain

data_public_as_stated.value: SV data and scripts public on ALMA Science Portal

evidence.quote: Detailed calibration scripts, preliminarily calibrated data products (i.e., without self-calibration), and self-calibration solutions for both continuum and spectral line data are available at the ALMA Science Portal

reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data, continuum fits and imaging recipe are numeric and redoable; the radiative transfer part is only partly reproducible.
